## 1. `prompt_cache_key` (decision D8)

**What changed.**

- **Where the key comes from.** `AgentRequest` gained `chat_key`. `AgentHost::make_agent_request` sets it to `<projectId>/<conversationId>`, for example `p-3f…9a-1c…77/c-2`. That is one added line in `AgentHost.cpp`, next to `request_id`.
- **How it reaches the codec.** `ProviderAgent::begin_transcript` copies it to `TurnTranscript::chat_key`.
- **What the codec sends.** `ResponsesCodec::build` sends it as `prompt_cache_key` on reply requests.

**Why a new field was needed.** The chat id was not available at the codec before. `request_id` contains the project and chat ids, but also the message id and attempt, so it changes on every turn.

**When no key is sent:**

- **Title requests.** They have no `chat_key`.
- **The account provider (JusPrin Cloud, `account_sign_in`).** See the gateway section.
- **Length.** A project id is at most 35 characters (`"p-"` plus two 64-bit hex numbers, `default_uuid()` in `ProjectPersistence.cpp`), so keys are about 40 characters. OpenAI's limit is undocumented. One community report says 64 characters; **unverified**.

**Tests.**

- `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, "every request of a chat carries one prompt_cache_key, and another chat another". It runs on the real host and loop. Chat A has a person turn with a slice call (two requests) and the app's turn after the slice. Chat B has one request. All three of chat A's requests carry `projectId/c-1`, and chat B's carries `projectId/c-2`.
- `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, "a request carries its chat's prompt_cache_key, except through JusPrin's gateway and for a title". It is a codec-level test covering:
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get the key
  - the gateway does not
  - a title request does not
  - an empty key sends nothing

The `[history-prefix]` guard compares every non-prompt body field across requests. It stays unchanged, which confirms that the key does not vary within a chat.

**OpenRouter.** Its Responses API reference lists `prompt_cache_key` as an accepted optional string, but does not say what it does. Whether OpenRouter forwards it to OpenAI is **unverified**.

### Gateway finding (verified by reading the source)

The gateway source is on this machine: `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise`, branch `master` at `7ab63cc151`, the same as `origin/master`. See `web_ent/jusprin/v2/upstream.py`.

- **Unknown fields are refused, not forwarded.** `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` is `model, store, stream, parallel_tool_calls, instructions, tools, input, reasoning`. `prepare()` answers any other top-level field with `400 invalid_request "Field "prompt_cache_key" is not allowed."`. Sending the key through the gateway would have failed every OpenAI-format JusPrin Cloud request. That is why the codec skips it for `account_sign_in`.
- **The gateway is where the key matters most.** Every JusPrin Cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation, and the gateway prepends the same identity line to `instructions`. So all cloud chats open identically and land on the same cache machines.
  - **Follow-up:** add `prompt_cache_key` to `ALLOWED_FIELDS['responses']` in tsd-enterprise and deploy it. Then drop `&& !profile.account_sign_in` in `ResponsesCodec::build`.
  - **Order matters:** the app change must not ship before the gateway one.
  - Whether the deployed gateway matches `master` is **unverified**. The plan says it went live 2026-10-25 as obi.4048.
- **Anthropic format.** `messages` are forwarded as sent, `cache_control` included, and the gateway's identity text goes in a block of its own before the client's `system` block. Only `metadata` is dropped.
- **For R2/R6.**
  - In-array `role: "system"` messages and `developer` items pass through untouched, because the gateway does not inspect `messages` or `input`.
  - The gateway sends upstream only its backend's configured headers (`_headers()` in `upstream.py`), never the client's.
  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

## 2. A stable tool list

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. The turn that attached a model therefore sent a different tool list from the turn before and the turn after. On Anthropic that means a cold cache for the whole chat, twice.
- A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.
- A call whose attachment could not be resolved failed with `not_found`: "The attached model is no longer available".

**Now.**

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.
- **Execution.** In `ToolExecutionCoordinator::execute`, an `attachmentId` that resolves to no stored model file fails with `invalid_arguments`, with the message: `No model file attached in this chat has the id "<id>". Nothing was imported. Use an attachment id from the person's message; if they attached no model file, ask them to attach it.`
- **Why `invalid_arguments`.**
  - It keeps the call in the "fix the call" group of `ToolErrors.hpp`, where `unknown_tool` already put it.
  - `not_found` means "read the state again, then call again", and re-reading the workspace cannot find an attachment.

## 3. The Anthropic cache breakpoint and skill text

**Where the breakpoints are today** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp`, all `{"type":"ephemeral"}`):

1. The last tool (`tools_json`, line 87).
2. The single `system` block (`build`, line 272).
3. The last block of the newest `user` message after role normalisation (`build`, line 262). It moves forward on every request.

A fired skill is sent as an in-array `role: "system"` message right after the user content or the tool results that fired it (`push_skills`). Its picture is a user image block, which merges into that user message, so the picture sits before breakpoint 3 and is cached. The skill text sits after it.

- On the request that fires it, the skill text is billed uncached at 1x.
- On the next request of the turn it is written to the cache at 1.25x.

That is M1's leak.

**Bytes after the last breakpoint, 26 recorded bodies.**

- **Method.** Each body was mapped to the Anthropic codec's message layout: developer items become system messages, then the codec's merge and normalisation rules apply. Then I counted the compact JSON after the breakpoint block.
- **Script.** `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin--claude-worktrees-cache-r8-f275c7/c449884d-06ef-4be3-ae77-8382bf117ba4/scratchpad/r8/after_breakpoint.py`, run as `python3 -I <script> tests/project_prompt/requests.json`.
- **Scope.** The system prompt and tools, about 41 KB, come before breakpoints 1 and 2 and are not counted.

| case | after the last breakpoint today (bytes) | of which skill text |
|---|---|---|
| model-imported-by-tool, model-opened-by-tool, model-opened-unnamed | 8,520 each | 8,446 (file-loaded) |
| advice-infill, answer-from-context, direct-change, issue-explain, issue-fix, loaded-vs-configured, reply-in-german, slice-warnings-ready, troubleshoot-first-layer | 5,309 each | 5,210 (print issues) |
| slice-refused-by-tool, slice-refused-then-ready | 3,640 each | 3,577 (slice failed) |
| after-intent | 1,329 | 1,288 (setup changed) |
| the other 11 cases | 0 | 0 |

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.
- With a breakpoint on the skill it would be 0 in every case.

**Why I did not move the breakpoint.** Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages page (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`), read 2026-10-29.

- **Under R2 it is an error.** R2 sends skills as turn-scoped messages (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`). The page says such a message carries "no `cache_control`" ("A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match"). The API answers `cache_control is not permitted on a turn-scoped system message` with a 400. It says to "Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead". Its agent-loop example puts it on the last `tool_result`. That is exactly today's breakpoint 3.
- **Today it is undocumented.** For a plain (`clear_at: "never"`) system message, the page says it "is itself cacheable", and that on the next turn "you can move your cache breakpoint past it". It never says `cache_control` is allowed on its blocks. Verifying that would need a live call, so I made none.

The rule was to change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's. Moving the breakpoint onto the skill is right under neither for certain, and is a 400 under R2. The code is unchanged.

**Recommendation for R2.**

1. **Keep breakpoint 3 where it is**, on the last block of the newest user message, which is the user turn before any skill. Never put `cache_control` on a turn-scoped message.
2. **The leak goes away under R2 without a breakpoint change.** The page says a turn-scoped message "renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it" and "A user message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts". A cleared message "costs no input tokens".
   - So under R2 a skill's text is billed once, on the request that fires it, and is never written to the cache.
   - Today the same text is billed at 1x, then written at 1.25x, then read on the turn's later requests.
   - The 81,950 bytes above stay after the breakpoint on the firing request, but stop being written to the cache one request late.
3. **The clearing request reads the right entry.** The page says that on the request that clears a message, "the reusable cached prefix ends at the user turn before it, so only the one assistant turn between that message and the new user message is reprocessed". The entry it reads is the one breakpoint 3 wrote on the firing request. That is another reason not to move breakpoint 3.
4. **A design point R2 must settle (behaviour, not cost).** Because a `tool_result` message clears a turn-scoped message, the model sees the skill only on the request that fired it, not "for the rest of the turn".
   - That matches what the Responses codec does today, since it drops the skill from the next request.
   - It does not match today's Anthropic codec, which keeps the skill visible for the rest of the turn.
   - If the plan's "cleared at the next user message" meant the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that.
5. **A message after a tool result on smaller models.** The plan already notes that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result. Under R2 that is the only place a skill fired by a result can go.

**TTL (decision D7).** Confirmed: the codec sends no `ttl`. `ephemeral()` is `{"type":"ephemeral"}` at all three breakpoints, so the 5-minute default applies. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` mentions `ttl` or `1h`. The gateway forwards `cache_control` unchanged.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## How I verified it

- **Catch2** `[request-log]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (appended at the end): two turns on the real host and provider loop, once per wire format, against the existing `RecordingProvider` fake. - **No live run.** No model was called. The Anthropic path is tested only through the Catch2 fake; the Responses path through the fake and the scripted harness run. - **For R2/R6.**

  - So R2's `clear_at` beta header (`anthropic-beta: mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`) reaches Anthropic only if it is added to the alias backend's `headers` in `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES`. Without it, `clear_at` is rejected as an unknown field.

**Before.**

- `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` offered `object_import` only when the request's message had an importable model attachment. - A call to `object_import` on any other turn was refused as `unknown_tool` before it ran.

- **Registry.** `object_import` has `ToolAvailability::Always`. `ImportableAttachment` is removed from the enum.

  - The "Ask the person" codes (`opened_before`, `workspace_unavailable`) mean other conditions.

- **`tests/shell/project_prompt_scenario.inc`.**
  - The prompt recorder used to strip `object_import` before comparing a request's tools with `project_tools.json`. It now compares directly.
  - It also leaves `prompt_cache_key` out of recorded bodies; that is commit `c5bd57c8eb`.

# Request-body logging (L0): report

Untracked working note, 2026-10-29. Branch `claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, commit `282342b918`, on top of `claude/chat-history-cache` (`cd4162fa97`). Not pushed or merged.

## Problem

The chat-history cache work has to check that each model request opens with the bytes of the one before it. No full request body was kept anywhere. The prompt-test recorder's `requests.json` holds bodies for its own suite, with stored results cut at 4,000 characters, and the live harness modes printed only token counts.

## What I built

- **`tests/jusprin_support/RequestLog.hpp`** (header-only, so the harness and `agent_bridge_tests` share it with no CMake change). `RequestLog::transport(provider, inner)` wraps any `IAgentHttpTransport`; `RequestLog::agent(inner)` wraps any `IAgentService`, so the log knows each request's purpose (reply or title), request id and attempt. For the n-th request of a run it writes:
  - `NNNN-request.json`: the body exactly as the transport was given it, written before it is forwarded.
  - `NNNN-request.meta.json`: provider, URL, headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key` and other credential headers redacted; `Idempotency-Key` kept), project id and chat id (chat ids restart in each project), purpose, request id, attempt, post time, body length.
  - `NNNN-response.sse`: the response stream as received.
  - `NNNN-response.json`: outcome (complete, error, cancelled, replaced, not_started), HTTP status, usage with the provider's own field names (Anthropic `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` come through as-is), stop reason, assembled text, error. It reads both the Messages and the Responses stream.
- **Shell harness flag `--request-log <dir>`**, for `--live-agent`, `--manual-live-agent` and `--project-prompt-requests`. It refuses a non-empty directory and any other mode (exit 2). Documented in the header comment of `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` (where all flags are documented; there is no `tests/shell/README.md`) and in a new section of `tests/project_prompt/README.md`.
- **`tests/project_prompt/prefix_check.py LOG_DIR [--ignore-key KEY] [--json]`**. For consecutive requests of the same project, chat and purpose it reports the common byte prefix, the first differing byte, the JSON path of that byte in each body, and the path of the last differing byte. `[append]` means the later body is the earlier one with items added at the end of one array and every other byte unchanged. `--ignore-key cache_control` drops Anthropic's moving breakpoint (then the bodies are compared as Python re-serialises them, and the output says so). Unit tests: `tests/project_prompt/test_prefix_check.py`.

## How I verified it

- **Catch2** `[request-log]` in `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` (appended at the end): two turns on the real host and provider loop, once per wire format, against the existing `RecordingProvider` fake. Each logged reply body equals the bytes the fake received; usage, stop reason, text, project and chat id, numbering and redaction are checked. I proved it can fail: making the logger append one byte to each body gave 4 byte-equality failures and 8 length failures; restored, it passes (150 assertions).
- **Whole agent suite**: 471 test cases, 16,575 assertions, all passed (Release build in this worktree).
- **`test_prefix_check.py`**: 9 tests pass. The "an append followed by a later change is not an append" test fails when the tail condition is removed.
- **Scripted harness run**: `--project-prompt-requests` on the `direct` conversation of `script.json` (two passes, scripted model, nothing sent over the network) with `--request-log` wrote 333 requests (1,332 files, largest body 1.4 MB). `prefix_check.py` reported all 329 pairs as `[append]` and took 7 seconds. The recorder's own output file was byte-identical with and without `--request-log`. `requests.json` and the baselines are untouched.

## What I could not verify, and things to know

- **No live run.** No model was called. The Anthropic path is tested only through the Catch2 fake; the Responses path through the fake and the scripted harness run. Real streams (OpenAI's `response.completed` usage, Anthropic's `message_start`/`message_delta` usage) follow the documented shapes the codecs already parse, but no real stream has gone through this logger yet.
- **The live harness mode only builds an OpenAI agent** on this branch. The Anthropic journey mode (`--plan-journey`) is uncommitted in `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch`; to log it, wrap its `make_openai_http_transport()` with `log.transport("anthropic", …)` and its agent with `log.agent(…)`, the same way `install_harness_agent` does.
- **Not logged**: the printer panel's Agent and any agent the host rebuilds through its chat model source (a chat that picks a model other than the one the harness installed). Both are built from the app configuration through `make_openai_http_transport()` in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Covering them needs a small seam in production code (for example a test-settable transport wrapper used by `make_openai_http_transport`); I did not add one.
- **Reading the byte count on OpenAI**: the app writes JSON keys alphabetically, so a Responses body opens with `input` and has `instructions` and `tools` after it. The shared byte count of a clean append is then just the earlier `input`; read the kind and the last-difference path, not the count. This is about the JSON byte order only. The order the provider caches in is its own and was not checked here.
- **Pre-existing harness failures, unrelated to this change**: the scripted run of the `direct` conversation reports `direct-change_ends_with_print-issues FAIL` and `direct-change_sent_once_0 FAIL`, with and without `--request-log`. The cause is not investigated; it means `script.json`'s expectation that the `direct-change` point carries the print-issues skill no longer holds on `claude/chat-history-cache`. Re-recording `requests.json` from this branch would hit it.

- 15 of 26 bodies have bytes after the breakpoint, totalling 81,950. In every case it is one trailing system message holding the skill.

**Why I did not move the breakpoint.** Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages page (`platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages`), read 2026-10-29.

- **Under R2 it is an error.** R2 sends skills as turn-scoped messages (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`). The page says such a message carries "no `cache_control`" ("A cleared message is never part of a cache key, so a breakpoint on it could never match"). The API answers `cache_control is not permitted on a turn-scoped system message` with a 400. It says to "Put the breakpoint on the last block of the preceding user turn instead". Its agent-loop example puts it on the last `tool_result`. That is exactly today's breakpoint 3.
- **Today it is undocumented.** For a plain (`clear_at: "never"`) system message, the page says it "is itself cacheable", and that on the next turn "you can move your cache breakpoint past it". It never says `cache_control` is allowed on its blocks. Verifying that would need a live call, so I made none.

The rule was to change the placement only if it is right under both today's behaviour and R2's. Moving the breakpoint onto the skill is right under neither for certain, and is a 400 under R2. The code is unchanged.

**Recommendation for R2.**

1. **Keep breakpoint 3 where it is**, on the last block of the newest user message, which is the user turn before any skill. Never put `cache_control` on a turn-scoped message.
2. **The leak goes away under R2 without a breakpoint change.** The page says a turn-scoped message "renders only while no `role: "user"` message comes after it" and "A user message that carries only `tool_result` blocks counts". A cleared message "costs no input tokens".
   - So under R2 a skill's text is billed once, on the request that fires it, and is never written to the cache.
   - Today the same text is billed at 1x, then written at 1.25x, then read on the turn's later requests.
   - The 81,950 bytes above stay after the breakpoint on the firing request, but stop being written to the cache one request late.
3. **The clearing request reads the right entry.** The page says that on the request that clears a message, "the reusable cached prefix ends at the user turn before it, so only the one assistant turn between that message and the new user message is reprocessed". The entry it reads is the one breakpoint 3 wrote on the firing request. That is another reason not to move breakpoint 3.
4. **A design point R2 must settle (behaviour, not cost).** Because a `tool_result` message clears a turn-scoped message, the model sees the skill only on the request that fired it, not "for the rest of the turn".
   - That matches what the Responses codec does today, since it drops the skill from the next request.
   - It does not match today's Anthropic codec, which keeps the skill visible for the rest of the turn.
   - If the plan's "cleared at the next user message" meant the next message from the person, `clear_at` does not do that.
5. **A message after a tool result on smaller models.** The plan already notes that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 may ignore a system message placed right after a tool result. Under R2 that is the only place a skill fired by a result can go.

**TTL (decision D7).** Confirmed: the codec sends no `ttl`. `ephemeral()` is `{"type":"ephemeral"}` at all three breakpoints, so the 5-minute default applies. Nothing in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` mentions `ttl` or `1h`. The gateway forwards `cache_control` unchanged.

All three sessions are done and reviewed. Nothing is merged yet; the branches wait for your OK.

**What each one delivered**

- **Deletions (R1 + R3a)** on `refs/heads/claude/cache-r1-r3a-7264fd`, two commits. Production diff is +1/−104 lines in `AgentHost.cpp`, all deletion. The session quoted both the deleted reminder and the standing-prompt sentence that already says it, with one correction: that sentence dates from e3f071d99a (2026-10-15), not 86f8395071. The agent suite passes. The guard test fails at the same count, as expected, but its first failure moved from the reminder to the workspace block and picture, which is what the next steps address.
- **Cache hygiene (R8)** on `refs/heads/claude/cache-r8-f275c7`, three commits. Production diff is +28/−10 across eight files: a `chat_key` carried from host to codec, `prompt_cache_key` sent on OpenAI and OpenRouter, `object_import` offered on every turn with a clean `invalid_arguments` failure when nothing is attached, and the `ImportableAttachment` enum value removed. Fail-first was proven on the tool-list test. The breakpoint was left in place with a written analysis.
- **Request logging (L0)** on `refs/heads/claude/cache-request-log-eca52c`, one commit, test code only. A `--request-log` flag writes each body byte-exact with its response usage, and `prefix_check.py` compares consecutive bodies. A scripted run logged 333 requests and every pair was a clean append.

**Three findings worth your attention**

1. **The JusPrin Cloud gateway refuses `prompt_cache_key`.** The R8 session read the gateway source in `tsd-enterprise` and found an allowlist of Responses fields. The app therefore skips the key for signed-in accounts, which is where it matters most, since every cloud user shares one OpenAI organisation. The fix is a gateway change first (add the field to the allowlist and deploy), then drop the condition in the app. The same reading showed in-array system messages pass through untouched, but client headers do not. R2's `clear_at` beta header has to be configured on the gateway's alias backend or it will fail.
2. **`clear_at` clears earlier than the design assumed.** Anthropic clears a turn-scoped message at the next user-role message, and a tool-result message counts. So under R2 a skill is visible only on the request that fired it, not for the rest of the turn. That matches today's OpenAI path and not today's Anthropic path. This needs a decision before R2 starts; it is recorded in the plan doc.
3. **A harness scenario is already broken on the integration branch.** L0 found two failures in the scripted `direct` conversation with and without its flag. The `direct-change` point no longer carries the print-issues skill. Re-recording `requests.json`, which R1 needs before the injection eval, will hit this.

Merging is mechanical: each branch merges cleanly onto cd4162fa97, and R8 and L0 both appended tests to the end of `test_agent_bridge.cpp`, so one conflict needs a hand resolution. The simplicity table in the plan doc now has the numbers for all three.

content.text:
Partly. For Anthropic Opus 5.5 there is enough to give a range; for OpenAI there is nothing.

**What the data says (Opus 5.5, six live chats, 9 to 17 requests each, prices from the batch's own cost script):**

| Chat | Actual cost | Same tokens with no cache | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| bunny (today's code) | $0.43 | $1.34 | 3.2x |
| plug (today's code) | $0.30 | $0.97 | 3.3x |
| vase (today's code) | $0.56 | $1.61 | 2.9x |
| bunny (prototype) | $0.32 | $1.22 | 3.8x |
| plug (prototype) | $0.23 | $0.76 | 3.2x |
| vase (prototype) | $0.51 | $1.70 | 3.3x |

So with caching off entirely, a chat costs about three times what it costs today, roughly $0.65 to $1.05 more per chat at these lengths. Today's cache already covers the 15,210-token system-and-tools prefix on every request, which is most of the input; the retelling problem we are fixing costs much less than that, about 20% of today's bill, not 200%.

**Caveats:**

- Six chats from three scripted journeys, all three to four person turns long. Longer chats grow the no-cache penalty roughly linearly, since every request resends everything.
- The journeys were run by a script, so the number of tool calls per turn is typical of those tasks, not of real users.
- No OpenAI data at all. OpenAI's cache discount is 90% for gpt-5.x and automatic, and its input prices are different, so the ratio will differ. The M4 baseline the harness session is about to record is the first OpenAI number we will have.
- "No cache" here means the provider's cache missing on every request, which is also roughly what a chat looks like after a pause longer than the 5-minute TTL.
